event_text: Åland War: The Battle of Suomenlinna begins.
headline: Russia Bombs Suomenlinna as Åland War Ignites
story: Barry gazed out at the smoke-shrouded fortress, "Ah, Suomenlinna, Susan. The Russians have decided to test the resolve of the Swedish-Finnish garrison. It's 1855, and the Åland War is officially underway. The British and French are watching with interest, of course – can't have the Russians gaining too much control over the Baltic." Susan cocked her head, "Yes, because nothing says 'diplomatic relations' like bombarding a strategic island fortress. The Russians have brought a fleet of 16 ships, if I'm counting correctly. I do hope the defenders have a sturdy insurance policy." Barry dryly noted, "The Russian admiral, General Berg, seems confident – claims he can take the fortress in a fortnight. I daresay the Swedes and Finns might have a thing or two to say about that." As the cannons roared, Susan commented, "And the Anglo-French fleet is... observing. From a safe distance, naturally. One wouldn't want to get too caught up in someone else's war, after all." Barry snorted, "Not when there are trade agreements to maintain and diplomatic niceties to observe."
regret_line: One wonders if the Russians would've reconsidered had they known the war would end with the Treaty of Paris, rendering their efforts rather moot.
winner_line: The war machine, naturally – more cannons to sell, more ships to build, more empires to prop up.
